sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Henrietta house best?
sections.html:
That depends on repairs and timing. A full listing, a sale you run yourself and an as-is cash purchase all work in this Rochester suburb, where roughly 70% of homes are occupied by their owners and the rest are rented.

Henrietta's midpoint home value of $223,700 sits far below the $640,800 figure for the Town of Hempstead, so a few thousand dollars of repairs or commission is a larger slice of what you take home. Price the work before you choose. A house needing only paint and a deep clean can go to market. One with a failing furnace, a wet basement or years of put-off upkeep may net about the same through a quick as-is sale.

  • Listing: the broadest exposure and typically the best price, offset by commission, repairs and a buyer's mortgage timeline.
  • By owner: the commission stays with you, as do the pricing, showings and contract details.
  • As-is cash: fewer steps and a closing day you can often set, at a price that absorbs the repairs.

Whichever way you lean, ask for each offer in writing, with the price, the date and each side's closing costs spelled out.

sections.h2: What is Henrietta like for a seller?
sections.html:
Henrietta is a town in southern Monroe County, about seven miles south of downtown Rochester. The Genesee River forms its western edge, Brighton lies to the north, Pittsford and Mendon to the east and Rush to the south. A short stretch of the Erie Canal crosses the northeast corner.

The town was formed in 1818 when residents of East and West Henrietta split from Pittsford over a dispute about the recording of deeds. The population grew from about 3,000 to about 14,000 in the decade after World War II as suburbs spread around Rochester. The New York State Thruway opened through town in 1954, Rochester Institute of Technology and the National Technical Institute for the Deaf moved to Henrietta in 1968, and Interstate 390 and the Marketplace Mall made it one of the main retail districts in Monroe County.

Today the town includes the hamlets of East Henrietta and West Henrietta and Riverton, a planned community set up in 1973. Rush-Henrietta Central School District serves it. For a seller, the pitch is practical: highway access to the Thruway and I-390, a short commute (17.6 minutes on average), and a campus and retail district that keep the town busy.

sections.html:

sections.h2: When are Henrietta property tax bills due, and where do I pay?
sections.html:
The Town Clerk's office acts as Receiver of Taxes and collects both the Combined Town and County bill and the school bill. The Combined bill is mailed on the last business day of December and is due by February 10. The school bill is mailed on the last business day of August, with full payment due October 1, or a first installment by September 15.

The town's payment page, updated November 3, 2026, says November 2 was the last day to pay the 2026-2027 school tax at Henrietta Town Hall. Any balance now goes to the Monroe County Treasurer, who cannot take school tax payments after November 18, and whatever remains after that is added to the 2027 Combined Town and County bill. That detail matters at a closing: confirm that the school bill shows paid in full so no leftover gets pushed onto the next owner's bill.

  • Town Clerk tax office: mail to Receiver of Taxes, Henrietta, P.O. Box 579, Henrietta, NY 14467; duplicate bills at 585-359-7035.
  • Monroe County Treasurer: 39 West Main Street, Room B-2, Rochester, NY 14614; phone 585-753-1200.
  • Online: Monroe County's Real Property Portal shows bills and payment history.

Mortgage escrow does not change the rules. If your lender pays your taxes, the lender gets the bill; if you paid off the loan, a Bank Code Removal Request Form makes sure the bill comes to you.

sections.h2: What does the Henrietta Assessor's Office do for sellers?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office prepares the annual assessment roll, runs the grievance and tax certiorari process, administers exemptions including STAR, and manages the town's continuous revaluation. The town's assessor is a New York State certified assessor appointed to a six-year term. The office phone is 585-359-7032.

Ask it two things before you list. First, which exemptions the house carries, since STAR appears only on the school bill. Second, whether your parcel is part of any exemption correction. A notice on the Assessor's page says that some limited-income senior and disability exemption holders may get corrected school tax bills, and that an increase would be added to the 2027-28 school bill. A buyer will want to know what the taxes will be after the sale, so ask the office what applies to a new owner.

For a grievance, contact the office early in the year for the current window and form.

sections.h2: What is the transfer tax, and where is the deed recorded?
sections.html:
The state charges $2 for every $500 of sale price, and sellers pay unless the contract shifts it. A house selling at the town's midpoint value of $223,700 would owe $896, from 448 units of $500.

The tax is reported on Form TP-584, and a residential sale of $1 million or more also owes a separate 1% tax paid by the buyer.

Deeds for Henrietta go to the Monroe County Clerk at 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614, open Monday through Friday from 9:00am to 5:00pm. The Clerk is the registrar of deeds, mortgages, satisfactions of mortgages, judgments and liens. Email is preferred for contact. Your closing attorney or title company normally files the deed.

sections.h2: What should I weigh between a cash sale and a listing in Henrietta?
sections.html:
Begin with what you would pocket, then add the calendar. A listing may reach a higher price but brings commission, repairs and a lender's approval window, while an as-is sale gives up some price for speed and certainty.

  • Confirm who covers the transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Ask for proof of funds and a closing date in writing.
  • Check the school and Town and County tax status with the Town Clerk or the Monroe County portal.
  • If tenants live in the house, ask the buyer how they will handle the lease.

faqs.q: When are Henrietta property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Combined Town and County bill is due February 10, and the school bill is due October 1 for full payment, with a first installment by September 15. Bills are mailed on the last business day of December and August.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Henrietta school tax balance now?
faqs.a: With the Monroe County Treasurer, at 39 West Main Street, Room B-2 in Rochester, phone 585-753-1200. The town said November 2 was its last day, and the county cannot accept school tax payments after November 18.

faqs.q: Who handles exemptions and assessment grievances in Henrietta?
faqs.a: The Town Assessor's Office, at 585-359-7032. It prepares the assessment roll, runs the grievance and tax certiorari process, and administers exemptions including STAR.

faqs.q: Who pays the New York transfer tax on a Henrietta sale?
faqs.a: The seller, at $2 per $500 of price, unless the contract moves it to the buyer. The buyer pays a separate 1% tax on residential sales of $1 million or more.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for a house in Henrietta?
faqs.a: At the Monroe County Clerk's Office, 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester. The Clerk is the registrar of deeds, mortgages, judgments and liens for the county.
